second_data_loss_vector.question_answered: Is the chosen route the same one `state.js:174` sits behind? YES.
second_data_loss_vector.mechanism: `lib/scheduler.js` `kickMember`'s compose calls `beginTaskAttempt(task, member)` → `lib/state.js` `activateTaskAttempt`, which sets `task.status='claimed'`, mints a new `attemptId` AND sets `task.output = undefined` (the line the wave records as L44(a) / t19's second data-loss vector). My delivery-boundary re-check runs AFTER that, so it can prevent the WAKE but never the WIPE.
second_data_loss_vector.measured: raw/output-wipe-probe.mjs — one `kickMember` on a task holding `output: "THE STORED DELIVERABLE (9000 bytes of findings)"` (status in_progress, attempt 1): after the kick the record reads `output: null`, `attempt: 2`, `status: claimed`, with 1 delivery. DETERMINISTIC, not a race: the compose rotates the attempt on every dispatched ticket.
second_data_loss_vector.consequence: A stored deliverable is destroyed by any re-dispatch of the task — including one my own re-check will then REFUSE, because the wipe happens at compose time and the refusal at the delivery boundary. T-46's append guarantee therefore has a second, independent hole that this task does NOT close.
second_data_loss_vector.where_the_fix_belongs: `lib/state.js` (`activateTaskAttempt`/`beginTaskAttempt`) — OUTSIDE t36's inScope. Two shapes, both needing their own test: (i) keep `output` when the new attempt belongs to the SAME generation (a re-dispatch of the same owner), or (ii) snapshot `output` before the compose and restore it in the refusal path when the task is terminal and its output is undefined. I did NOT implement either: (ii) inside scheduler.js would be an untestable-in-process repair on a path the race cannot steer, and (i) is another file's contract.
second_data_loss_vector.row: Already tracked as plan §8 L44(a); this measurement adds that it fires on EVERY composed ticket, not only a completed re-dispatch.
